top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B044) rests on one identifiable originating model, Melitz 2003, with the separable Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple extension on exporting versus foreign direct investment. It moved trade analysis from the industry to the firm. More than twenty years of firm-level evidence from many countries has confirmed its qualitative predictions on selection and reallocation. The remaining dispute concerns welfare magnitudes, which depend on Pareto and CES assumptions. A citation worded around the mechanism and not the magnitudes handles that. The credit boundary is imperfect: Bernard, Jensen, Eaton and Kortum, and Redding, fall outside a two-name award. I judge that a cost of the cap and not a sign the discovery is poorly bounded. It is a later advance distinct from the 2008 recognition. P002 (Autor, Hanson and Katz) is important and mature, but I rank it second because of its unstable boundary. It is either one labour-demand discovery or two strands, so the third name is Katz or Dorn. China-shock persistence and shift-share identification are still debated, and the task framework has contributors outside the ballot. Either proposal is better than no award, since both rest on mature, important work.
recusal_note: No tie to Melitz or Helpman appears in my profile. I co-authored with Timo Boppart (co-opted member, P002 supporter) and John Hassler (chair, P001 supporter), and I am secretary. My work on capital-skill complementarity and inequality is adjacent to P002's field. I disclose these ties and do not treat them as evidence of merit. No recusal is adjudicated.
